```{r data-import}

df <- filter(raw_data, A2PA <= "Active")
```

# 1 · The sample (row 1, column 2)

```{r sample-palette}
# Poster palette. Athlete / Enthusiast / Active carry the group colours used in
# every panel; everything below the third level is greyed to mark exclusion.
pal  <- c(Athlete = "#22415C", Enthusiast = "#D19A2E", Active = "#3F8E8C")
grey <- "#6E7C8C"
ink  <- "#1E2833"
hair <- "#C3D2DE"

# Row fills are the same hues mixed 15 % over white. col2rgb() returns colours
# in COLUMNS, rgb() wants them in ROWS, hence the transpose.
tint <- function(x, p = 0.15) {
  grDevices::rgb(t(p * grDevices::col2rgb(x) + (1 - p) * 255), maxColorValue = 255)
}
```

```{r sample-table}
# All five A2PA levels, including the two that the analyses exclude.
sample_rows <-
  raw_data |>
  summarise(
    N    = n(),
    Age  = sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", mean(Age,  na.rm = TRUE), sd(Age,  na.rm = TRUE)),
    # Education is a column now rather than a source note. Computed on raw_data
    # like the rest of the row, so the excluded identities get a value too;
    # a group with no education recorded shows an em dash rather than NaN.
    Edu = {
      p <- 100 * mean(Education == "higher", na.rm = TRUE)
      if (is.finite(p)) sprintf("%.0f %%", p) else "\u2014"
    },
    MMSE = sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", mean(MMSE, na.rm = TRUE), sd(MMSE, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .by  = A2PA
  ) |>
  arrange(A2PA) |>
  mutate(A2PA = as.character(A2PA))

# Accent per row: palette for the analysed levels, grey for the rest.
n_keep <- length(pal)
accent <- c(unname(pal), rep(grey, nrow(sample_rows) - n_keep))
fills  <- tint(accent)

sample_rows
```

```{r sample-gt}
tab_sample <-
  sample_rows |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_label(
    A2PA = "A2PA identity",
    N    = "N",
    Age  = "Age",
    # Two lines, so the column names itself and needs no note to explain what
    # the percentage is of.
    Edu  = gt::html("Higher<br>education"),
    MMSE = "MMSE"
  ) |>
  gt::cols_align("left",  columns = A2PA) |>
  gt::cols_align("center", columns = c(N, Age, Edu, MMSE)) |>
  # Without explicit widths gt sizes the columns to their content and centres
  # the result, so the table sat in the middle of the slot with a white gutter
  # either side. These sum to 100 %, which with table.width = pct(100) makes the
  # table span the panel.
  gt::cols_width(
    A2PA ~ gt::pct(26),
    N    ~ gt::pct(9),
    Age  ~ gt::pct(22),
    Edu  ~ gt::pct(21),
    MMSE ~ gt::pct(22)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(color = grey, weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_column_labels()
  )

# Row-wise colour coding. A left rule in the full-strength hue carries the code
# even in greyscale; the fill is a quiet second cue.
for (i in seq_len(nrow(sample_rows))) {
  tab_sample <-
    tab_sample |>
    gt::tab_style(
      style = list(
        gt::cell_fill(color = fills[i]),
        gt::cell_text(color = if (i <= n_keep) ink else grey)
      ),
      locations = gt::cells_body(rows = i)
    ) |>
    gt::tab_style(
      style = list(
        gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
        gt::cell_borders(sides = "left", color = accent[i], weight = gt::px(10))
      ),
      locations = gt::cells_body(columns = A2PA, rows = i)
    )
}

tab_sample <-
```

# 2 · The activity ladder (row 2, column 1)

```{r activity-ladder-plot}
# ---- 2 · The activity ladder (row 2, column 1) -------------------------------

## ---- r ladder-data ----
pa_levels <- c(
  "Current PA (WHO)",
  "Current PA (excl. walking, chores)",
  "Current PA (excl. walking, chores, gardening)"
)

# NOTE: WHO is the demanding criterion: it needs BOTH moderate-or-intense
# intensity AND >= 2.5 h/week. The other two need only > 0 hours, at any
# intensity of a progressively narrower list of activity types.
pa_label <- c(
  "WHO-recommended\nphysical activity",
  "Any PA excluding\nwalking and chores",
  # NOTE: strip text does not wrap, it clips. At this facet width 24 pt bold
  # fits about 20 characters per line, so both lines are kept under that.
  "Any PA excluding\nthose plus gardening"
)

ladder <-
  df |>
  select(A2PA, all_of(pa_levels)) |>
  pivot_longer(-A2PA, names_to = "measure", values_to = "meets") |>
  mutate(meets = as.integer(as.character(meets))) |>
  summarise(k = sum(meets), n = n(), .by = c(A2PA, measure)) |>
  mutate(
    # Wilson score interval = prop.test(correct = FALSE);
    # Wald is unusable here because 91/92 pushes its upper limit past 100 %.
    p  = 100 * k / n,
    lo = 100 * map2_dbl(k, n, \(k, n) prop.test(k, n, correct = FALSE)$conf.int[1]),
    hi = 100 * map2_dbl(k, n, \(k, n) prop.test(k, n, correct = FALSE)$conf.int[2]),
    m_i   = match(measure, pa_levels),
    label = factor(pa_label[m_i], levels = pa_label),
    A2PA  = factor(as.character(A2PA), levels = names(pal))
  )

## ---- r ladder-tests ----
ladder_tests <-
  ladder |>
  arrange(m_i, A2PA) |>
  summarise(tab = list(cbind(yes = k, no = n - k)), .by = c(m_i, measure)) |>
  arrange(m_i) |>
  mutate(
    chi     = map(tab, \(t) suppressWarnings(chisq.test(t))),
    X2      = map_dbl(chi, \(x) unname(x$statistic)),
    dfree   = map_dbl(chi, \(x) unname(x$parameter)),
    p_chi   = map_dbl(chi, \(x) x$p.value),
    min_exp = map_dbl(chi, \(x) min(x$expected)),  # < 5 invalidates the approximation
    p_fish  = map_dbl(tab, \(t) fisher.test(t)$p.value)
  )

# APA-style bounded statistic: strip the leading zero.
no0 <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x))
}
fmt_p  <- function(p) if (p < .001) "*p* < .001" else sprintf("*p* = %s", no0(p, 3))
fmt_x2 <- function(i) {
  with(ladder_tests[i, ],
       sprintf("&#967;<sup>2</sup>(%d) = %s, %s", dfree, no0(X2, 1), fmt_p(p_chi)))
}

## ---- r ladder-plot ----
FAM <- "Helvetica Neue"
Y0  <- 50
SHP <- c(Athlete = 21, Enthusiast = 22, Active = 24) # secondary encoding

# Facets whose chi-square clears .05 get the same tinted panel as the delayed
# recall facet in R2, so "this is where the difference is" reads the same way in
# both results panels.
ladder_band <-
  ladder_tests |>
  filter(p_chi < .05) |>
  transmute(label = factor(pa_label[m_i], levels = pa_label))

ladder_finding <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "**A2PA identity indicates what the women do, not how much.**",
    "Meeting the WHO-recommended level does not separate the groups (%s);",
    "doing any activity beyond walking and chores does (%s),",
    "and excluding gardening widens the gap (%s)."
  ),
  fmt_x2(1),
  fmt_x2(2),
  fmt_x2(3)
)

ladder_how <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "All three panels score the same %d women. The WHO criterion counts at least",
    "2.5 h/week of moderate or vigorous activity of any type; the other two count",
    "any amount at any intensity, of a narrowing list of types. Dots are",
    "proportions, bars 95%% Wilson intervals, axis truncated at %d%%. Smallest",
    "expected count is %s, in the middle panel; Fisher's exact test agrees there",
    "(*p* = %s)."
  ),
  sum(ladder$n[ladder$m_i == 1]),
  Y0,
  no0(ladder_tests$min_exp[2], 1),
  no0(ladder_tests$p_fish[2], 3)
)

p_ladder <-
  ggplot(
    ladder,
    aes(x = A2PA, y = p, colour = A2PA)
  ) +
  # Drawn first, so everything else sits on top of it. Semi-transparent for the
  # same reason as in R2: an opaque fill would blank out the panel gridlines,
  # which ggplot draws in the background layer.
  geom_rect(
    data = ladder_band,
    aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fill = tint(ink, 0.16),
    alpha = 0.5,
    colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_linerange(
    aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
    linewidth = 2.8,
    alpha = 0.45,
    lineend = "round"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = A2PA, shape = A2PA),
    size = 8.5,
    colour = "white",
    stroke = 1.8
  ) +
  # Every point is labelled BELOW its own interval. Labels to the right of the
  # marker collide whenever two adjacent groups have similar proportions, which
  # is exactly what happens in the first and third panels.
  geom_text(
    aes(y = lo, label = sprintf("%.0f %%", p)),
    vjust = 1.6,
    size = 22 / .pt,
    fontface = "bold",
    colour = ink,
    family = FAM
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ label,
    nrow = 1
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = pal,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = pal,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = SHP,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  # Wider padding pulls the three markers toward the middle of their facet: with
  # 3 categories the spacing is 1 unit out of (2 + 2 * add), so raising `add`
  # tightens the group.
  scale_x_discrete(
    expand = expansion(add = c(1.4, 1.4))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(Y0, 100),
    breaks = seq(Y0, 100, 10),
    labels = \(v) paste0(v, " %"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.05))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "% of group meeting the criterion",
    caption = paste(ladder_finding, ladder_how)
  ) +
  # colour, fill and shape all map to A2PA, so ggplot merges them into one
  # legend; override.aes must be given once or it warns about duplication.
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 9, stroke = 1.8))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 26,
    base_family = FAM
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = hair, linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.spacing.x    = unit(26, "pt"),
    strip.text   = element_text(
      size = 24,
      face = "bold",
      colour = ink,
      lineheight = 1.15,
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(b = 12)
    ),
    axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(colour = grey, size = 24),
    axis.title.y = element_text(colour = grey, size = 24, margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.ticks   = element_blank(),
    # Bottom-centre of the plotting region, which is the middle facet.
    # ggplot2 >= 3.5 wants legend.position = "inside" + legend.position.inside.
    # Just clear of the 50 % rule. The axis floor is Y0 with a 3 % expansion, so
    # that gridline sits at about 0.028 of panel height; the legend's opaque
    # background would cover it from any lower.
    legend.position      = c(0.5, 0.04),
    legend.justification = c(0.5, 0),
    legend.direction     = "horizontal",
    # Transparent, not white: with facets shaded the opaque box cut a white
    # notch out of the tint. The keys and text are bold enough to sit over a
    # gridline unaided.
    legend.background    = element_blank(),
    legend.key           = element_blank(),
    legend.text   = element_text(size = 26, face = "bold", colour = ink),
    legend.margin = margin(4, 8, 4, 8),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    # Wrapping caption, following the ECVP builder's two-tier convention.
    plot.caption = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(
      size = 19, colour = grey, family = FAM, lineheight = 1.25,
      margin = margin(t = 14), halign = 0
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(6, 10, 4, 4)
  )

p_ladder
```

# 3 · Cognition (row 2, column 2)

```{r cognition-plot}
# ---- 3 · Cognition (row 2, column 2) -----------------------------------------

## ---- r cognition-data ----
# The four domains that define SuperAging. Memory first: it is the finding.
z_levels <- c("z(RAVLT-DR)", "z(TMT-B)", "z(BNT-30)", "z(Animal naming)")
z_label  <- c("Delayed recall", "TMT-B", "BNT-30", "Animal naming")

domains <-
  df |>
  select(A2PA, all_of(z_levels)) |>
  pivot_longer(-A2PA, names_to = "domain", values_to = "z") |>
  filter(!is.na(z)) |>
  mutate(
    d_i    = match(domain, z_levels),
    domain = factor(z_label[d_i], levels = z_label),
    A2PA   = factor(as.character(A2PA), levels = names(pal))
  )

# Mean and 95 % CI per group and domain, following the convention of the
# earlier COSACTIW poster: violin = distribution, dot = mean, bar = 95 % CI.
domain_mean <-
  domains |>
  summarise(
    m  = mean(z),
    se = sd(z) / sqrt(n()),
    n  = n(),
    .by = c(domain, A2PA)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    lo = m - qt(.975, n - 1) * se,
    hi = m + qt(.975, n - 1) * se
  )

# SuperAging prevalence
sa <-
  df |>
  summarise(
    k     = sum(SA == "1", na.rm = TRUE),
    n     = sum(!is.na(SA)),
    n_all = n(),
    .by   = A2PA
  ) |>
  mutate(
    p  = 100 * k / n,
    lo = 100 * map2_dbl(k, n, \(k, n) prop.test(k, n, correct = FALSE)$conf.int[1]),
    hi = 100 * map2_dbl(k, n, \(k, n) prop.test(k, n, correct = FALSE)$conf.int[2]),
    A2PA = factor(as.character(A2PA), levels = names(pal))
  )

## ---- r cognition-tests ----
# One-way ANOVA per domain with Tukey HSD post-hoc
domain_tests <-
  domains |>
  nest_by(domain) |>
  mutate(
    fit  = list(aov(z ~ A2PA, data = data)),
    tidy = list(summary(fit)[[1]]),
    `F`  = tidy[["F value"]][1],
    df1  = tidy[["Df"]][1],
    df2  = tidy[["Df"]][2],
    p    = tidy[["Pr(>F)"]][1],
    pw   = list(TukeyHSD(fit)$A2PA)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(domain, `F`, df1, df2, p, pw)

sa_test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(cbind(sa$k, sa$n - sa$k)))

# Pairwise p-values for the memory domain, Enthusiast against the other two.
# TukeyHSD names rows "<second>-<first>" in factor-level order.
mem_pw <- domain_tests$pw[[1]]
stopifnot(all(c("Enthusiast-Athlete", "Active-Enthusiast") %in% rownames(mem_pw)))
p_ath  <- mem_pw["Enthusiast-Athlete", "p adj"]
p_act  <- mem_pw["Active-Enthusiast", "p adj"]

# Vectorised: these are called inside mutate() over all four domains.
fmt_p  <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "*p* < .001", sprintf("*p* = %s", no0(p, 3)))
fmt_F  <- function(i) {
  with(domain_tests[i, ],
       sprintf("*F*(%d, %d) = %s, %s", df1, df2, no0(F, 2), fmt_p(p)))
}

## ---- r cognition-plot ----
# Tukey contrasts for delayed recall, printed under the violins of the group
# each one compares Enthusiasts WITH, and in that group's colour. No brackets:
# the lines cost the violins about a third of their height, and their labels
# then had to be staggered so far apart that the pairing was no longer legible.
# Colour and position carry the pairing instead, at a cost of one z unit.
mem_p <- data.frame(
  domain = factor(z_label[1], levels = z_label),
  A2PA   = factor(c("Athlete", "Active"), levels = names(pal)),
  # Pulled in from x = 1 and 3: centred on the outer violins the right-hand
  # label ran off the panel edge. Still unambiguously left half / right half.
  x      = c(1.25, 2.75),
  lab    = sprintf("p = %s", no0(c(p_ath, p_act), 3))
)

# The one domain that separates the groups gets a tinted panel, so the eye lands
# on it before it reads any label.
mem_band <- data.frame(domain = factor(z_label[1], levels = z_label))

# Pairwise differences in SuperAging prevalence, with Newcombe-style intervals
# from the same prop.test family as the proportions themselves.
CL <- 1 - 0.05 / 3   # Bonferroni level for three pairwise contrasts

sa_pairs <- data.frame(
  a = c("Enthusiast", "Enthusiast", "Athlete"),
  b = c("Athlete", "Active", "Active")
) |>
  mutate(
    lab = paste(a, "-", b),
    d   = map2_dbl(a, b, \(a, b) {
      i <- match(c(a, b), sa$A2PA)
      100 * (sa$k[i[1]] / sa$n[i[1]] - sa$k[i[2]] / sa$n[i[2]])
    }),
    # Bonferroni level for the three contrasts, so "interval excludes zero" IS
    # the adjusted test and the colour cue cannot contradict the geometry.
    lo = map2_dbl(a, b, \(a, b) {
      i <- match(c(a, b), sa$A2PA)
      100 * prop.test(sa$k[i], sa$n[i], correct = FALSE, conf.level = CL)$conf.int[1]
    }),
    hi = map2_dbl(a, b, \(a, b) {
      i <- match(c(a, b), sa$A2PA)
      100 * prop.test(sa$k[i], sa$n[i], correct = FALSE, conf.level = CL)$conf.int[2]
    }),
    sig = lo > 0 | hi < 0
  ) |>
  mutate(lab = factor(lab, levels = rev(lab)))

p_sa <-
  ggplot(
    sa,
    aes(x = A2PA, y = p, colour = A2PA)
  ) +
  geom_linerange(
    aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
    linewidth = 2.8,
    alpha = 0.45,
    lineend = "round"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = A2PA, shape = A2PA),
    size = 7.5,
    colour = "white",
    stroke = 1.6
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.0f %%", p)),
    nudge_x = 0.22,
    hjust = 0,
    size = 22 / .pt,
    fontface = "bold",
    colour = ink,
    family = FAM
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = pal,
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = pal,
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = SHP,
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 1.1))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = \(v) paste0(v, " %"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.18, 0.18))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    subtitle = "SuperAging"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 24,
    base_family = FAM
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = hair, linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(colour = grey, size = 20),
    axis.ticks   = element_blank(),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 23,
      face = "bold",
      colour = ink,
      margin = margin(b = 6),
      hjust = 0.5
    )
  )

p_sa_diff <-
  ggplot(
    sa_pairs,
```

```{r health-table}
# ---- 4 · Health and mental activity (row 3, column 1) -----------------------

## ---- r health-spec ----
health_spec <- tibble::tribble(
  ~var,                ~kind,   ~dir, ~block,
  "GDS-15",            "cont",   -1L, "Mental health",
  "GAI-SF",            "cont",   -1L, "Mental health",
  "FAQ",               "cont",   -1L, "Mental health",
  "Subj. health",      "cont",   +1L, "Subjective health",
  "Mental activities", "cont",   +1L, "Mental activity",
  "BMI",               "cont",   -1L, "Metabolic and lifestyle risk",
  "Hypertension",      "bin",    -1L, "Metabolic and lifestyle risk",
  "Diabetes",          "bin",    -1L, "Metabolic and lifestyle risk",
  "Smoking",           "bin",    -1L, "Metabolic and lifestyle risk",
  "Alcohol",           "bin",    -1L, "Metabolic and lifestyle risk"
) |>
  mutate(
    block = factor(block, levels = unique(block)),
    var   = factor(var, levels = var)
  )

## ---- r health-data ----
# Binary measures may arrive as 0/1, as "0"/"1", or as No/Yes; anything else is
# an error rather than a silent coercion.
to01 <- function(x) {
  u <- sort(unique(as.character(x[!is.na(x)])))
  if (all(u %in% c("0", "1"))) {
    as.integer(as.character(x))
  } else if (all(tolower(u) %in% c("no", "yes"))) {
    as.integer(tolower(as.character(x)) == "yes")
  } else {
    stop("Unrecognised binary coding: ", paste(u, collapse = "/"), call. = FALSE)
  }
}

health <-
  df |>
  # Self-rated health is stored high = poor; 6 - level puts it with the rest.
  mutate(`Subj. health` = 6 - as.numeric(`Subj. health`)) |>
  select(A2PA, all_of(as.character(health_spec$var))) |>
  # Columns arrive as a mix of numeric, factor and character, so pivot through
  # character and parse per measure below rather than asking vctrs to unify them.
  pivot_longer(
    -A2PA,
    names_to = "var",
    values_to = "raw",
    values_transform = as.character
  ) |>
  left_join(health_spec, by = "var") |>
  filter(!is.na(raw)) |>
  mutate(v = if (kind[1] == "bin") to01(raw) else as.numeric(raw), .by = var) |>
  mutate(
    var  = factor(var, levels = levels(health_spec$var)),
    A2PA = factor(as.character(A2PA), levels = names(pal))
  )

health_n <-
  health |>
  summarise(n = n(), .by = var)

## ---- health-tests ----
# Omnibus test per measure, native to the measure: one-way ANOVA for the
# continuous ones, chi-square for the binary ones. Deliberately unadjusted as
# the claim here is mostly of ABSENCE, and multiplicity correction only makes a
# null easier to obtain, so adjusting would be arguing in our own favour.
health_tests <-
  health |>
  nest_by(var, kind) |>
  mutate(
    p = if (kind == "cont") {
      summary(aov(v ~ A2PA, data = data))[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]
    } else {
      suppressWarnings(chisq.test(table(data$A2PA, data$v))$p.value)
    }
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(var, kind, p) |>
  mutate(
    lab = ifelse(p < .001, "p < .001", paste0("p = ", no0(p, 3))),
    sig = p < .05
  )

## ---- r health-effects ----
# Eta-squared: the share of a measure's variance accounted for by identity. For
# a 0/1 outcome this is the natural analogue of the continuous case and is on
# the SAME scale, which is what lets both kinds share one column.
eta2 <- function(y, g) {
  a <- anova(stats::lm(y ~ g))
  a[["Sum Sq"]][1] / sum(a[["Sum Sq"]])
}

health_es <-
  health |>
  summarise(est = eta2(v, A2PA), .by = var) |>
  mutate(eta = sub("^0\\.", ".", sprintf("%.3f", est)))

## ---- r health-table-data ----
tab_rows <-
  health |>
  summarise(
    txt = if (kind[1] == "bin") sprintf("%d (%.0f %%)", sum(v), 100 * mean(v))
          else                  sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", mean(v), sd(v)),
    .by = c(block, var, kind, A2PA)
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = A2PA,
    values_from = txt
  ) |>
  left_join(
    select(health_es, var, eta),
    by = "var"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    select(health_tests, var, lab, sig),
    by = "var"
  ) |>
  arrange(var) |>
  mutate(
    block = as.character(block),
    var = as.character(var)
  ) |>
  select(
    block,
    var,
    all_of(names(pal)),
    eta,
    lab,
    sig
  )

grp_n <-
  df |>
  count(A2PA) |>
  tibble::deframe()

## ---- r health-caption ----
# The headline is a claim and is written by hand; it must be re-checked against
# the numbers whenever the freeze changes. Everything after it is generated, so
# the sentence cannot contradict the table.
HEADLINE <- "**The groups are mostly comparable across health measures.**"

andify <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) <= 1) return(paste(x, collapse = ""))
  paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])
}

sig_i  <- order(health_tests$p)[seq_len(sum(health_tests$sig))]
null_p <- health_tests$p[!health_tests$sig]

health_finding <- paste(
  HEADLINE,
  if (length(sig_i) == 0) {
    sprintf(
      "None of the %s measures differs significantly across the three identities (all *p* > %s).",
      english(nrow(health_tests)),
      no0(min(null_p), 2)
    )
  } else {
    sprintf(
      "Of the %s measures, %s %s significantly between the identities (%s); the other %s %s not (*p*%s > %s).",
      english(nrow(health_tests)),
      andify(as.character(tolower(health_tests$var[sig_i]))),
      if (length(sig_i) == 1) "differs" else "differ",
      paste(gsub("^p", "*p*", health_tests$lab[sig_i]), collapse = "; "),
      english(length(null_p)),
      if (length(null_p) == 1) "does" else "do",
      if (length(null_p) == 1) "" else "s",
      no0(min(null_p), 2)
    )
  }
)
```

|---|---|---|
| `panel-s1-sample` | Sample & measures | 1298, 577 |
| `panel-r1-activity` | R1 · activity ladder | 148, 1501 |

```{r export-spec}
# Panel slot in the A0 template, in points. The sheet is 2383 x 3370 pt and each
# of the six panels has a 937 x 791 pt picture area beneath its title bar.
SLOT_W_PT <- 937
SLOT_H_PT <- 791

SLOT_W_IN <- SLOT_W_PT / 72  # 13.014 in = 330.6 mm
SLOT_H_IN <- SLOT_H_PT / 72  # 10.986 in = 279.1 mm

# Raster factor for the two gt tables and for the PNG previews. 4 x 72 = 288 dpi
ZOOM <- 4

# gt tables as vector PDF
TABLE_PDF <- TRUE

OUT_DIR <- here::here("outputs", "2026-psychologicke-dny-poster", "panels")
dir.create(OUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r export-fonts, echo=FALSE}
# FAM is "Helvetica Neue" and graphics devices substitute SILENTLY when a family
# is missing, so a wrong font would only show up on the printed poster.
if (requireNamespace("systemfonts", quietly = TRUE)) {
  matched <- systemfonts::match_font(FAM)
  if (!grepl("helvetica", matched$path, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    warning(
      "Font '", FAM, "' not found; the device will substitute ", matched$path,
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
}

# cairo_pdf embeds glyph outlines, so the PDF carries the typeface with it. The
# default pdf() device only references the font by name and lets the print shop
# substitute, which is exactly the failure we cannot see until it is printed.
HAS_CAIRO <- isTRUE(capabilities("cairo"))
if (!HAS_CAIRO) {
  warning(
    "No cairo device: writing PNG only. The 288 dpi rasters are fine ",
    "for A0, but the vector route is preferable.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}
```

```{r export-helpers}
# PNG header reader. IHDR stores width and height as big-endian 4-byte integers
# at offsets 16 and 20. Dependency-free, and measures the file that was actually
# written rather than trusting the call that wrote it.
png_dim <- function(path) {
  con <- file(path, "rb")
  on.exit(close(con))
  readBin(con, "raw", 16L)
  c(
    w = readBin(con, "integer", 1L, size = 4L, endian = "big"),
    h = readBin(con, "integer", 1L, size = 4L, endian = "big")
  )
}

# ggplot panels. Place the PDF in Keynote, because it stays sharp at any
# enlargement. The PNG serves as a preview and a fallback.
export_plot <- function(plot, name) {
  png_path <- file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0(name, ".png"))
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    png_path, plot,
    width = SLOT_W_IN,
    height = SLOT_H_IN,
    units = "in",
    dpi = 72 * ZOOM,
    bg = "white"
  )
  if (HAS_CAIRO) {
    pdf_path <- file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0(name, ".pdf"))
    ggplot2::ggsave(
      pdf_path,
      plot,
      device = grDevices::cairo_pdf,
      width = SLOT_W_IN,
      height = SLOT_H_IN,
      units = "in",
      bg = "white"
    )
    c(pdf_path, png_path)
  } else {
    png_path
  }
}

# gt tables. Write the HTML, pin the page box to the slot, and photograph the
# page rather than the table.
export_table <- function(tab, name, pdf = TABLE_PDF) {
  html <- file.path(tempdir(), paste0(name, ".html"))
  path <- file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0(name, ".png"))
 
  gt::gtsave(tab, html)
 
  # min-height, not height: a table that fits pads out to exactly the slot, and
  # one that does not produces a taller image that export-verify can flag. A
  # fixed height with overflow:hidden would clip it silently instead.
  css <- sprintf(paste0(
    "<style>html,body{margin:0;padding:0;width:%dpx;min-height:%dpx;",
    "background:#ffffff;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;text-size-adjust:none}",
    "table{width:%dpx !important;margin:0 !important}",
    # The min-height exists only so a short table pads out to the slot in the
    # SCREENSHOT. In print the page is already the slot, and a body pinned to
    # exactly the page height spills onto a second page on any sub-pixel
    # rounding. text-size-adjust is Chrome's print text inflation, which
    # enlarges the source notes but not the table body.
    "@media print{html,body{min-height:0}}</style>"
  ), SLOT_W_PT, SLOT_H_PT, SLOT_W_PT)
 
  x <- readLines(html, warn = FALSE)
  hit <- grep("</head>", x, fixed = TRUE)
  if (length(hit) != 1L) {
    stop("Could not find a single </head> in the gt export for ", name,
         "; the CSS pin was not applied.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  x[hit] <- sub("</head>", paste0(css, "</head>"), x[hit], fixed = TRUE)
  writeLines(x, html)
 
  webshot2::webshot(
    url = html, file = path,
    vwidth = SLOT_W_PT, vheight = SLOT_H_PT,
    zoom = ZOOM, expand = 0, selector = "body"
  )
 
  if (!isTRUE(pdf) || !requireNamespace("pagedown", quietly = TRUE)) {
    return(path)
  }

  # pdftools is REQUIRED, not optional. Print layout is fractionally taller than
  # screen layout, so a table that fits the screenshot can still spill onto a
  # second page -- and page 2 is invisible once page 1 is placed in Keynote.
  # Worse, gt puts source notes in <tfoot>, which Chrome keeps with the LAST
  # page: the overflow shows up as missing BODY ROWS while the notes still look
  # correct. Without a page count that failure is undetectable, so we refuse to
  # write a PDF we cannot check.
  if (!requireNamespace("pdftools", quietly = TRUE)) {
    warning(
      "pdftools is not installed, so ", name, ".pdf cannot be checked for ",
      "silent overflow onto a second page. Writing PNG only.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
    return(path)
  }

  pdf_path <- file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0(name, ".pdf"))

  # scale = k * 96/72 makes one CSS px one point, because the design is sized in
  # px and the screenshot route makes 1 px = 1 pt (the viewport is SLOT_W_PT px
  # wide). Print media does not work that way on its own: a CSS px is 1/96 in,
  # so without the 96/72 the table lands at 75 % of the slot. printBackground is
  # needed because Chrome omits background paint from print, which would drop
  # every tinted cell and every coloured column rule.
  print_pdf <- function(out, k, h_in) {
    pagedown::chrome_print(
      input = html, output = out, verbose = 0,
      options = list(
        paperWidth = SLOT_W_IN, paperHeight = h_in,
        marginTop = 0, marginBottom = 0, marginLeft = 0, marginRight = 0,
        scale = k * 96 / 72, printBackground = TRUE
      )
    )
    out
  }

  # Measure rather than guess: print onto a page four times too tall, so there
  # is no pagination, and read the lowest piece of text off it. That gives the
  # print-layout content height directly, in points, at 1 px = 1 pt.
  probe <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
  on.exit(unlink(probe), add = TRUE)
  words <- pdftools::pdf_data(print_pdf(probe, 1, 4 * SLOT_H_IN))[[1]]
  need <- if (nrow(words)) max(words$y + words$height) else NA_real_

  # A percent or two of shrink is invisible at A0. Much more than that and this
  # panel's type no longer matches the others, which is worse than a raster.
  k <- if (is.finite(need)) min(1, SLOT_H_PT / need) else 1
  MIN_K <- 0.95

  if (k < MIN_K) {
    warning(
      name, ": print layout needs ", round(need), " pt of the ", SLOT_H_PT,
      " pt slot, so it would have to shrink to ", round(100 * k), " %. That is ",
      "too far to match the other panels. PDF not written -- place the PNG, or ",
      "cut about ", ceiling((need - SLOT_H_PT) / 26), " lines of source note.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
    return(path)
  }

  print_pdf(pdf_path, k, SLOT_H_IN)
  np <- pdftools::pdf_info(pdf_path)$pages

  # Belt and braces: the measurement is of text only, so a stray border can
  # still tip a borderline table over. Step down until it is one page.
  while (!identical(as.integer(np), 1L) && k > MIN_K) {
    k <- k - 0.01
    print_pdf(pdf_path, k, SLOT_H_IN)
    np <- pdftools::pdf_info(pdf_path)$pages
  }

  if (!identical(as.integer(np), 1L)) {
    unlink(pdf_path)
    warning(name, ": still ", np, " pages at ", round(100 * MIN_K),
            " %. PDF not written; place the PNG.", call. = FALSE)
    return(path)
  }

  if (k < 1) {
    message(name, ".pdf: content at ", round(100 * k),
            " % to keep it on one page.")
  }
  c(path, pdf_path)
}
```

```{r export-run}
exported <- c(

  export_plot(p_ladder,    "panel-r1-activity"),

  export_table(tab_health, "panel-r3-health")
)

exported
```

```{r export-verify, echo=FALSE}
fit <-
  tibble::tibble(path = exported[grepl("\\.png$", exported)]) |>
  mutate(
    dim  = map(path, png_dim),
    file = basename(path),
    w_pt = map_dbl(dim, "w") / ZOOM,
    h_pt = map_dbl(dim, "h") / ZOOM,
    w_pc = round(100 * w_pt / SLOT_W_PT),
    h_pc = round(100 * h_pt / SLOT_H_PT)
  ) |>
  select(file, w_pt, h_pt, w_pc, h_pc)

fit

over <- fit$file[fit$h_pt > SLOT_H_PT]
if (length(over)) {
  warning(
    "Taller than the ", SLOT_H_PT, " pt slot: ", paste(over, collapse = ", "),
    ". Shorten a source note, or drop data_row.padding by a pixel.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
} else {
  message("All four panels fit the ", SLOT_W_PT, " x ", SLOT_H_PT, " pt slot.")
}
```
